payload.answer: When a job is stuck, mis-aimed, or burning credits on the wrong thing -- the operator watching a session go somewhere useless and having no button. Stop marks it CANCELLED so it will not be retried, and lets the current lease drain rather than yanking it: the worker finishes the turn in hand and claims no more. That is not a new mechanism to invent -- the SIGTERM drain added for Kubernetes scale-in already does exactly this, and stop should reuse the concept rather than grow a second one. The job stays in history; the ledger is append-only and a stopped job is evidence, not an embarrassment to erase.
